stem: Methanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$, is soluble in water because it forms hydrogen bonds with water molecules.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Draw a fully labelled diagram to show how a hydrogen bond forms between a water molecule and a methanol molecule.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Methanol has a melting point of $-97.6^{\circ}\text{C}$ and a boiling point of $64.7^{\circ}\text{C}$.

A sample of pure liquid methanol is added to a flask and then sealed. The sealed flask is left for several days at constant temperature. The vapour pressure is then measured as $17\text{ kPa}$.
parts.text: Describe what is meant by the term *vapour pressure of methanol*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why some of the liquid becomes a vapour.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest and explain why the vapour pressure of water at room temperature is lower than the vapour pressure of methanol at room temperature. Refer to the correct intermolecular forces in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
Methanol is made by reacting carbon monoxide with hydrogen.

$$\text{CO(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{OH(g)}$$

Carbon monoxide and hydrogen react at $1.0 \times 10^7\text{Pa}$ and $200^{\circ}\text{C}$. Eventually the reaction mixture reaches dynamic equilibrium.

The table shows the amounts of each species present in the mixture.

|  | $\text{CO(g)}$ | $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ | $\text{CH}_3\text{OH(g)}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| initial amount/mol | 1.0 | 2.0 | 0 |
| equilibrium amount/mol | 0.030 | 0.060 | 0.97 |
parts.text: Explain what is meant by *dynamic equilibrium*.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the partial pressure of methanol vapour at equilibrium under these conditions. Show your working.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Write an expression for the equilibrium constant, $K_{\text{p}}$, for this reaction. State the units in your answer.
